newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sugar tariff cut seen costly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sugar tariff cut seen costly.

text.p: The Queensland sugar industry was likely to lose A$20 million a year with the removal of the import tariff on raw and refined sugar, Harry Bonanno, chairman of grower organisation CANEGROWERS, said on Friday.
Bonanno called on Australia's government to cut tariffs on industries which produce farm inputs and drive costs.
Removal of the tariff would allow the Australian consumer to purchase sugar at the world's lowest prices, he said in a statement.
But while the sugar industry was set to lose its tariff on raw and refined sugar, the car industry continued to be protected by a 22.5 percent tariff, he said.
Bonanno's comments follow the handing down of a government report earlier this month which recommended the abolition of Australia's A$55.00 a tonne tariff on imported sugar, effective July 1, 1997.
